podcast.body: Greenbaum, who is Jewish, was inspired to write this song after hearing country star Porter Wagoner sing "Pastor Absent on Vacation" on television. He felt that the "love generation fizzled out into revolution, but I think some people really wanted to believe in something." The song was notable for its distinctive fuzz tone, produced by a fuzz box built directly into his Fender guitar. Background vocals were provided by the Stovall Sisters, a gospel trio from Oakland, California. It reached number three on the Billboard Hot 100 in April 1970. "He took Spirit in the Sky to number three on the Billboard Hot 100 in April 1970."
